quotes.text: If [your Radar plan](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works.md#compare-plans) supports this feature, you can create lists of specific types of information and use them in [rules](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules.md).
Each list can contain up to 50,000 items.
entries on default fingerprint allowlists have a maximum lifespan of 30 days.
You can create custom payment method fingerprint lists with longer or indefinite expiration windows for your custom rules.

old_evidence.text: Stripe Radar for Fraud Teams lets you create lists of specific types of information and use them in [rules](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules.md).

findings: The May 10, 2026 capture names Radar for Fraud Teams for creating custom lists in rules, adding Dashboard items and longer-lived payment-method fingerprint lists (old 8,88,108). The November 7, 2026 capture (raw line 2) uses supporting-plan terminology at raw line 9, merges Dashboard view/add/remove at raw line 86 and omits the repeated tier name at raw line 104. These are substantive documentation changes in entitlement framing, not proof of a product rename, equivalent plans or universal access. The November linked How Radar works matrix 15–38 lists default allow/block absent on Lite and supported Standard/Plus/Pro, with custom rules/backtesting/allow/block lists on Plus/Pro only. It is scoped plan matrix evidence rather than a specific account check. Current source 13 and concept 59 need dating and distinction between default and custom lists.

Both guides describe values referenced by Radar rules to trigger a configured allow, block or review action, with default lists by Cards, ACH and SEPA that permit item additions/removals but cannot be edited/deleted as lists (old 8–58, new 9–56). Fingerprints are card or bank account identifiers, and first email/domain picks Charge then Card or Bank Account then Customer, depending on rail. Current source 17–19 broadly preserves categories and distinctions.

Both overview custom inventories contain ten bullet entries (old 62–73, new 60–71); source 21, concept source-list annotation 269, Stripe index 524 and wiki/companies/stripe.md line 721 label 11 while source 23 lists ten. The list guide is not a complete current API enum: November Create a value list schema 55–69 lists 12 values including account and crypto_fingerprint, with the API's us_bank_account_fingerprint name. Scoped April 22 Dahlia changelog 1–15 attributes account item type to Connect platforms. This discrepancy is overview vs API scope, not evidence of a new count in the November overview or blanket Dashboard support for API-only types.

Both guides retain merchant creation via Dashboard or Value List API with alias auto-generated and overridable in Dashboard, selecting item type, and explicitly adding a rule reference. Custom lists can be edited or removed. Dashboard item history tracks value/author/date and up to 50,000 items. String items added in Dashboard can expire and are no longer evaluated by rules. Default fingerprint allowlist entries have at most 30 days; longer or indefinite lifespan applies to custom payment-method fingerprint lists for custom rules, not arbitrary custom list types (old 75–90,104–108; new 73–86,100–104; source 25–31 and concept 63).

For card payments, refund-and-report as fraudulent or Charge update fraud_details.user_report=fraudulent populates default fingerprint/email blocklists, including other cards on the Customer where applicable and email sources listed (old 92–102, new 88–98). This is a consequential default-list state change, separate from a generic refund or an account-wide request outcome. New link points from risk-evaluation to transaction-risk-prevention, whose scoped 163–174 preserves fraud feedback for refund and associated email/fingerprint. Word changes, blank table rows, list numbering and changed API link label are presentational/navigation.

source_assessments.reason: November changes eligibility framing and linked authority. Independently correct the 11-type count and overbroad indefinite-expiration claim while preserving May and newer plan and API distinctions.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/lists, November 7, 2026 documents plan-conditioned list use in Radar rules. Stripe supplies default Card, ACH and SEPA lists whose items can change while the lists cannot be edited or deleted. An eligible merchant creates a custom typed list in Dashboard or the Value List API and references it in a rule; the rule action can allow, block or review matching payments. Items can be filtered and limits are 50,000 per list. Dashboard string-item expiry stops rule use, default fingerprint allowlist entries last at most 30 days, and custom payment-method fingerprint lists in custom rules may have longer or indefinite windows. Card fraud report or the documented Charge update populates default fingerprint/email blocklists (old raw lines 8-58 and 62-108, new raw lines 9-56 and 60-104). source-stripe-radar-lists.md broadly preserves May behavior but its claimed count of 11 conflicts with both guides' ten bullets, and expiration scope is broader than the raw. The separate November plan matrix distinguishes default Standard/Plus/Pro and custom Plus/Pro support, while the API enum has additional values. Neither creates entitlement or verifies an actual rule outcome.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/lists, November replaces the May 10, 2026 Radar for Fraud Teams references with supporting-plan wording for creation, Dashboard item management and custom fingerprint expiry. That is substantive documentation framing, with no inferred universal access or specific rename. The November plan matrix scopes default and custom entitlements separately. Default categories, ten overview types, 50,000-item and 30-day boundaries, custom fingerprint lifespan and card fraud feedback stay dated and intact (old raw lines 8-20 and 62-108, new raw lines 9-21 and 60-104). The November API list includes account and crypto_fingerprint beyond the guide, so source-stripe-radar-lists.md should correct the overview count while preserving scoped API and Connect version evidence. Blank table rows, punctuation, step numbers and risk feedback link destination are presentation or navigation. Preserve May raw provenance, root-to-Stripe index and reciprocal Radar concept/source routes, and the separate risk-evaluation, transaction-risk, plan and REST support references.
